caption_proposed_v6: \caption{\textbf{Spanning-tree overlap mostly reads the one-nearest-neighbor scale (Proposition~\ref{prop:mst}).} Vision--language pairs on the preregistered pool of $m=2047$ WIT inputs with prh\_clip+l2, at mid depth (open markers) and the last layer (filled). The nearest-neighbor forest $F_A$ of the language model lies inside its MST (Proposition~\ref{prop:mst}), and the bridges are the tree edges outside $F_A$. (a) MST overlap $s_{\Tset}$ against one-nearest-neighbor overlap $s_{N,1}$, one point per pair, with the bound of Proposition~\ref{prop:mst} (black line), the region it excludes (shaded), the diagonal (dotted) and chance (cross). (b) Share of the shared MST edges that lie in $F_A$, one dot per pair, with the median (black bar), the share expected if the shared edges were a random subset of the language-model tree (dashed), and the preregistered level (grey line). (c) Bridge overlap minus its permutation null mean against BLOOMZ parameter count (log scale), averaged over vision models, with $95\%$ bootstrap intervals over vision models and the median per-pair $95\%$ permutation quantile (grey band). $\mathrm{Tr}$ is the preregistered trend statistic; with five sizes no exact $p$-value can fall below the printed floor, so the trend test is power-limited. The Spanning Trees paragraph of Appendix~\ref{app:exp-s12} and Table~\ref{tab:app-pe2} give the values and both pools.}

caption_v8.tex: \caption{\textbf{Spanning-tree overlap mostly reads the one-nearest-neighbor scale, and the bridges exceed their null without an established size trend (Proposition~\ref{prop:mst}).} Vision--language pairs of WIT at mid depth (open) and the last layer (filled). (a) MST overlap against one-nearest-neighbor overlap for each pair. (b) Per pair, the share of the shared MST edges that lie in the nearest-neighbor forest of the language model, with its value for a random subset of tree edges (null). (c) Bridge overlap minus its permutation null mean along BLOOMZ, as means over vision models with $95\%$ intervals. Table~\ref{tab:app-pe2} gives the values.}
